title: Richard Sterban, the Oak Ridge Boys bass singer behind "Elvira", dies at 83
summary: His deep "oom papa mow mow" helped make the 1981 song one of country music's biggest hits.
body:
Richard Sterban, the bass singer of the Oak Ridge Boys for more than five decades, has died at the age of 83. His family and the band announced that he died on Saturday 14 November in Hendersonville, Tennessee.

Sterban joined the group in 1972. His deep bass line on "Elvira" in 1981 became one of the most recognisable sounds in country music and helped turn the song into a crossover hit.

Tributes

The Oak Ridge Boys were inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2015. The Hall of Fame described Sterban as "a foundational figure" in country music.

He had stepped back from touring with the group last year, but attended the Hall of Fame's medallion ceremony in October.

Sources: Variety, The Hollywood Reporter, WKRN.
